core: Marketing a hospitality business (hotel, restaurant, or brand), not a place
The services marketing mix: the 7 Ps (product, price, place, promotion, people, process, physical evidence)
Attribution: the original 4 Ps to E. Jerome McCarthy; the marketing-mix concept to Neil Borden; the three extended service Ps to Booms & Bitner (1981)
STP: market segmentation (geographic, demographic, psychographic, behavioral), targeting, and positioning
Distribution channels: direct booking vs intermediaries (OTAs, GDS, wholesalers) and the direct-vs-OTA cost trade-off
Digital, social, and content marketing; online reviews and online reputation

Commission ranges and the economics of shifting share to direct channels

Service-quality theory such as SERVQUAL and the IHIP characteristics (owned by Customer Service)

claims.claim: The marketing mix is the set of tactical tools a firm uses to influence demand; its most familiar form is the 4 Ps: product, price, place, and promotion.
The 4 Ps framework is credited to marketing professor E. Jerome McCarthy, who distilled Neil Borden's broader 'marketing mix' concept into four categories.
Booms and Bitner (1981) extended the mix to seven Ps for services by adding people, process, and physical evidence, arguing the four-P model fit tangible goods better than services.

STP (segmentation, targeting, positioning) is a customer-driven strategy: divide the market into segments, choose which to serve, and position the offering in target customers' minds relative to competitors.
Common consumer segmentation bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic (lifestyle, values, personality), and behavioral (usage, occasion, benefits sought).

In hospitality distribution, guests book either direct (hotel website, app, phone, front desk) or through intermediaries such as online travel agencies (OTAs), global distribution systems (GDS), and wholesalers.

As of 2026, OTA commissions typically run about 15-30%+ of the booking value (up from roughly 10% a decade earlier), while a direct booking carries no OTA commission (only the property's own marketing and payment-processing costs), so shifting share to direct channels raises net revenue per booking.
Online reviews and ratings are a major influence on travel and accommodation booking decisions, making online reputation management part of hospitality marketing.

Hospitality is a service business built on helping guests feel welcome; because the core product is an intangible experience, it is marketed with an extended services approach rather than only the goods-oriented 4 Ps.

sourceRecords.title: Principles of Marketing, Section 1.2: The Marketing Mix and the 4Ps of Marketing
sourceRecords.notes: Read live via WebFetch 2026-08-19. Supports the definition of the marketing mix and the four Ps: product ('the good or service that the company provides'), price ('what the consumer pays'), place ('where the product is purchased'), and promotion ('advertising, sales, and other communication efforts... to attract the customer'). Search-index extract of the same page attributes the 4 Ps to Professor E. Jerome McCarthy, who simplified Neil Borden's marketing-mix concept. The page footer states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; treated REFERENCE_ONLY and only facts/definitions used, prose original.

sourceRecords.title: Principles of Marketing, Chapter 5: Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning (Section 5.1)
sourceRecords.provider: OpenStax (Rice University); section read via the Business LibreTexts mirror
sourceRecords.notes: Chapter summary read live via WebFetch; Section 5.1 (segmentation bases) read via the Business LibreTexts OpenStax mirror (https://biz.libretexts.org/.../05:_Market_Segmentation_Targeting_and_Positioning/5.01) because that section rendered cleanly there. Supports the STP model (segment, target, position as the major elements of a customer-driven strategy), the definition of market segmentation ('dividing a target market into smaller, more precisely defined groups... expected to respond similarly to a marketing action'), and the four consumer segmentation bases: geographic, demographic, psychographic (lifestyle/values/personality, AIO, VALS), and behavioral (usage, occasion, benefits sought). OpenStax page footer states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (the LibreTexts mirror labels it CC BY 4.0); recorded the more restrictive license, used REFERENCE_ONLY, prose original.

sourceRecords.title: Booms, B. H., & Bitner, M. J. (1981). Marketing Strategies and Organization Structures for Service Firms, in Marketing of Services (Donnelly & George, eds.), pp. 47-51
sourceRecords.provider: American Marketing Association; bibliographic record verified via Semantic Scholar and Scientific Research Publishing reference records

Donnelly & George, American Marketing Association, Chicago, pp. 47-51. Used only to attribute the three extended service Ps (people, process, physical evidence) that Booms & Bitner added to McCarthy's 4 Ps for services marketing. Attribution fact only; no text of the work reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: A Guide to OTA Commission Rates in 2026
sourceRecords.notes: Read live via WebFetch 2026-08-19. Secondary, self-interested industry source. Supports: OTA commissions typically 15-30%+ of booking value in 2026 (up from ~10% a decade ago); direct bookings carry zero OTA commission but incur the property's own SEM/SEO/metasearch/paid-social costs; commission structures include merchant, agency, and blended models; and a cited cancellation differential (OTA ~21.8% vs direct ~10.6%). Figures dated 2026 and attributed; no wording reproduced. Corroborated on the general 15-30% range by independent trade coverage (Mews, Little Hotelier).
